leetcode-sql-50.title: LeetCode — SQL 50
leetcode-sql-50.authority: Defines lesson ORDER and the L1/L2 tier boundary. If this sheet and an overlay disagree on where a concept belongs, this sheet wins.
leetcode-sql-50.analogue: Striver A2Z — ordered, finite, judge-backed, the thing you finish.

hackerrank-sql-58.title: HackerRank — SQL track
hackerrank-sql-58.authority: Repetition only. Never introduces a concept the spine has not already introduced.
hackerrank-sql-58.analogue: Babbar FINAL450 — breadth and reps, weaker ordering.
hackerrank-sql-58.urlCaveat: Per-challenge slugs are not recorded; each entry links to its subdomain listing. Open by title.

leetcode-advanced-sql-50.title: LeetCode — Advanced SQL 50
leetcode-advanced-sql-50.authority: Defines the L3 tier boundary once enumerated.
leetcode-advanced-sql-50.blockedOn: LeetCode Premium. Enumerate from the account, then append with sheet='leetcode-advanced-sql-50'.

datalemur.title: DataLemur — SQL Interview Questions
datalemur.authority: Supplies company tags (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Netflix, Uber, LinkedIn, banks) and hard analytics problems. Never reorders the curriculum.
datalemur.filterHint: Filter category=SQL, difficulty=Hard, then tag by skill (window functions, CTEs, joins).

stratascratch.title: StrataScratch — real company SQL questions
stratascratch.authority: Same role as DataLemur; use for the modules DataLemur under-serves (time-series, geo, cohort).

pgexercises.title: PGExercises
pgexercises.authority: Fills the dialect-specific and recursive gaps the judge-backed sheets skip.

reference-ankit-bansal.title: Ankit Bansal — SQL / analytics SQL
reference-ankit-bansal.authority: None over ordering. Cited per-module for intuition on window functions, self-joins and analytics framing.

reference-techtfq.title: techTFQ (Thoufiq Mohammed) — SQL tutorials
reference-techtfq.authority: None over ordering. Cited per-module for CTEs, recursion and query-writing method.

rules: A sourced problem is never invented. Every entry carries platform + ref + url, or it does not go in this file.
tier is assigned by THIS curriculum, not by the platform's difficulty label. difficulty is recorded as provenance only.
The spine fixes order. An overlay may add reps at a tier but may not introduce a concept ahead of the spine.
A module's lesson may cite a sourced problem only if problems.json lists it for that module at that tier.
Synthesised drills stay legal and stay in the lesson files, but must be labelled platform='drill' so the origin is never ambiguous.
